claim: SEP raises average selection accuracy from 0.754 to 0.826 on HumanEval+ and 0.565 to 0.647 on LiveCodeBench at N=10 across seven models without learned verifiers.
stance_target: verification-utility baselines exist as selection methods, not confidence
quoted_support: At N = 10, SEP improves average accuracy from 0.754 to 0.826 on HumanEval+ and from 0.565 to 0.647 on LiveCodeBench
numbers: best or tied-best in 40 of 42 settings

breadth.confidence_families: not present (searched: confidence, calibrat, ECE); selection by symbolic functional agreement
breadth.model_families_and_sizes: seven models, 4B-20B: Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, Qwen3-14B, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, gpt-oss-20b and others (Sec 4.1.2, Tables 1-2)
breadth.base_vs_instruct: Qwen3-4B vs Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 appear in tables but not as a studied factor
breadth.reasoning_models: mix of reasoning and non-reasoning (Sec 4.1.2); settings in Appendix E
breadth.contamination_split: LiveCodeBench described as 'a contamination-resistant benchmark of recent contest-style programming problems'; no own release-date split
breadth.calibration_metrics: selection accuracy vs Pass@1 and Pass@10 only

claim: Consensus can fail because models produce correlated wrong solutions, which bounds agreement-based confidence in code.
quoted_support: consensus alone is not sufficient for correctness, because models can also produce correlated wrong solutions that implement the same mistaken behavior.
